subproblem.title: Where a represented current vanishes on an open set, its weight θH^n⌞M vanishes (fundamental lemma)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, W ⊆ ℝ^P, let T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Suppose W is open, W ⊆ U, and T vanishes on W (T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ W). Then R.measure(W) = 0, where R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → T.VanishesOn W → R.measure W = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 3, the consequence 'T vanishes on W ⇒ μ_T(W) = 0' of Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–768), which Simon states without proof. We use the parent's own alternative: test the fundamental lemma against a basis of the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors.
Uses: sibling unit_orientation_nonzero_bounded, i.e. every unit orientation ξ_0 of a subspace satisfies ξ_0 ≠ 0 and ‖ξ_0‖ ≤ 1.
Notation: ν := H^n⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M; μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity(x ↦ θ(x)); Λ^n := Covector (Euclid P) n; Λ_n := MultiVector P n = (Λ^n)*.

1. Orientation facts μ-a.e. Since μ is a withDensity measure of ν, μ ≪ ν (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous). By R.orients, for ν-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. By the sibling lemma, ξ(x) ≠ 0 and ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1 for ν-a.e. x, hence for μ-a.e. x.

2. Local finiteness. Let K ⊆ U be compact. Then K is closed, hence Borel, and
 μ(K) = ∫⁻_K θ dν = ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞
 (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, R.locallyIntegrable_mult).

3. Scalar components. For α ∈ Λ^n put f_α(x) := ξ(x)(α) ∈ ℝ.
 (a) f_α is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. ξ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient), and the evaluation L ↦ L(α) is continuous on Λ_n (continuous_eval_const). So f_α is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable), hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable (mono_ac, μ ≪ ν).
 (b) |f_α(x)| ≤ ‖ξ(x)‖·‖α‖ ≤ ‖α‖ for μ-a.e. x (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm and step 1).
 (c) Let K ⊆ W be compact. Then K ⊆ U, so μ(K) < ∞ by step 2, and by (a) and (b) f_α is integrable on K (IntegrableOn.of_bound). Since W is open (hence locally closed) and ℝ^P is locally compact, f_α is locally integrable on W (locallyIntegrableOn_iff).

4. Distributional identity. Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W, and let α ∈ Λ^n.
 - The form ω(y) := g(y)·α is C^∞ (g times a constant), compactly supported (HasCompactSupport.smul_right), and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ U. So ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ W, and T(ω) = 0.
 - By the representation and linearity of ξ(y),
 0 = T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(y)·ξ(y)(g(y)α) dH^n(y) = ∫ θ(y)·(g(y)·f_α(y)) dν(y).
 - θ is ℕ-valued and measurable, so the density of μ is y ↦ ((θ(y) : ℝ≥0) : [0,∞]) with y ↦ (θ(y) : ℝ≥0) measurable. Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul (which has no integrability hypothesis) gives ∫ g·f_α dμ = ∫ θ(y)·(g(y)·f_α(y)) dν(y).
 Hence ∫ g(y)·f_α(y) dμ(y) = 0.

5. Fundamental lemma. Apply the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations on the open set W for the Borel measure μ on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P (Mathlib IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero, real-valued case). It needs only the local integrability on W from 3(c) and the identity of step 4; no local finiteness of μ is required. So for every α ∈ Λ^n: for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ ξ(x)(α) = 0.

6. Λ^n is finite-dimensional. Let e_1,…,e_P be the standard basis of ℝ^P. The linear map
 α ↦ (α(e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(n)}))_{I : {1..n}→{1..P}} ∈ ℝ^{P^n}
 is injective, because an alternating n-linear map is determined by its values on tuples of basis vectors (Mathlib Module.Basis.ext_alternating). So Λ^n is linearly isomorphic to a subspace of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^{P^n}, hence finite-dimensional (Module.Finite.of_injective). Fix a basis α_1,…,α_N of Λ^n (Module.finBasis).

7. Apply step 5 to the finitely many covectors α_1,…,α_N and intersect the resulting full-measure sets (ae_all_iff). For μ-a.e. x: if x ∈ W, then ξ(x)(α_k) = 0 for k = 1,…,N.

8. Conclusion. Let x satisfy step 7 and step 1 (μ-a.e. x does), and suppose x ∈ W. Then the linear map ξ(x) : Λ^n → ℝ vanishes on a basis of Λ^n, so ξ(x) = 0 (Basis.ext applied to the underlying linear map). This contradicts ξ(x) ≠ 0 from step 1. Hence μ-a.e. x satisfies x ∉ W, i.e. μ(W) = 0 (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem).

Remark: a countable dense subset D of the finite-dimensional normed space Λ^n works equally well in steps 6–8 (TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense; ξ(x) vanishes on D and hence on closure D = Λ^n by continuity). One may also apply the Banach-valued fundamental lemma once to x ↦ ξ(x) ∈ Λ_n, since (∫ gξ dμ)(α) = T(gα) = 0.
Formalization note: in this contract Lean does not synthesize ContinuousENorm (MultiVector P n), so Integrable and LocallyIntegrableOn statements for MultiVector-valued maps do not elaborate directly. The scalar route of steps 3–8 avoids this.
proof_key_steps: μ = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ ≪ H^n⌞M, so by R.orients and the sibling lemma ξ ≠ 0 and ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1 hold μ-a.e.; also μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U.
Each scalar component f_α = ξ(·)(α) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, bounded by ‖α‖, and locally integrable on the open set W.
For g ∈ C^∞_c with tsupport g ⊆ W: ∫ g·f_α dμ = ∫_M θ·ξ(gα) dH^n = R.action(gα) = T(gα) = 0 (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul).
Fundamental lemma on W (IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero): f_α = 0 μ-a.e. on W, for every α.
Λ^n is finite-dimensional (injective evaluation on basis tuples); testing on a basis gives ξ(x) = 0 for μ-a.e. x ∈ W.
This contradicts ξ ≠ 0 μ-a.e., so μ-a.e. x lies outside W, i.e. μ(W) = 0.

audit.reason: Prose and type include all required hypotheses through IMRep, representation, openness of W, inclusion in U, and vanishing. Absolute continuity transfers orientation facts; compact-set finiteness establishes scalar local integrability. Smooth scalar tests and the density identity justify the fundamental lemma. The explicit finite-dimensional basis argument combines the almost-everywhere conclusions without an uncountable-intersection gap. Only the declared orientation child is needed; openness of U and compact closure of W are unnecessary.
